issue.title: fix(server): wait for terminal checkpoints before new messages

issue.body: A follow-up message can edit files before the previous turn's checkpoint captures them. Slow pull request lookups can extend that window. Track terminal events before logging or runtime consumers receive them. The application owns one capture service shared by the provider and both reactors. Hold new messages for that thread until capture succeeds, skips, or fails. Reserve the known active turn before an interrupt returns. Keep git status and pull request refresh work outside the capture worker. Active-turn steering still goes through. A second stop cancels messages waiting for capture. Capture failures and non-git projects do not block the next message. Verified after restacking with 195 focused server tests, the server typecheck, and targeted lint. The two new ordering tests fail on current main because the next turn edits files before capture. One existing real-Codex test requires a local binary and was skipped. This covers known terminal events and explicit interrupt ordering. It does not make native turn admission atomic with terminal events that arrive during send preparation, or change ambiguous interrupt error recovery. Stacked on [#10120](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/10120) to keep the related server changes in merge order. Created with Codex. Updated with Codex. > [!NOTE] > ### Wait for terminal checkpoint capture before starting next provider message > - Adds `TurnCheckpointCapture` service in [TurnCheckpointCapture.ts](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/10297/files#diff-3f3c85190d213b207bc99f3fcfecca6c20fb7f57e2ac9909021a9ae1fac3b2ee) to track per-thread pending captures for terminal provider events (completed/aborted) and interrupt reservations > - `ProviderService.publishRuntimeEvent` in [ProviderService.ts](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/10297/files#diff-b9b9384b78856ff56cff5dd0ccb106054fb5d2d1b7500fcd30d8938ebfec5775) now observes events through `TurnCheckpointCapture` before canonical logging and PubSub publication; `interruptTurn` and `stopSession` register interrupt expectations before adapter calls > - `ProviderCommandReactor` in [ProviderCommandReactor.ts](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/10297/files#diff-0630e9ad70d5dcd1c8586d29297f9b7d5f5436cc8e10fc88dc22acc511f1450d) holds turn-start requests for a thread with pending checkpoint capture and resumes them via internal `capture-ready` inputs once the capture completes; cancellation commands remove delayed requests and still invoke the provider interrupt or stop > - `CheckpointReactor` in [CheckpointReactor.ts](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/10297/files#diff-79dc41615f79575ae1404bd102df915797fb24ba34989557f80e229d305521fb) delegates completed/aborted event handling to `processTurnCompletion`, which signals `TurnCheckpointCapture.complete` on exit and moves Git status refresh to a separate drainable worker > - Behavioral Change: `ProviderService` construction now requires `TurnCheckpointCapture`; `RuntimeCoreDependenciesLive` in [server.ts](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/10297/files#diff-a8f34e8f17024480f0ca046c8ea4a8af3b525fe68940b703ba496fa4aa4ddfbd) provides it, and all test layers updated to include it > > > > Macroscope summarized 42e41b3. > >

comments.body:
> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 **Claude Fable 5.1 responding on behalf of Theo**

Closing in favor of #10347, which extracts the statusRefreshWorker split so checkpoint capture no longer waits behind the remote PR lookup. That closes most of the window on its own. The remaining cross-reactor gate (TurnCheckpointCapture threaded through ProviderService, both reactors and server.ts, plus the delayed turn start queue and interrupt reservations) adds a fourth coordination map to an 1800-line reactor and new user-visible stop behavior for a residual window of one git write-tree. Not worth that surface right now.
